opex.notes: Amounts taken from the most recent period column (12 months to Sep 2026, column E). Expenses include 5% non-recoverable VAT; unaudited, cash basis. No district cooling, collection loss or vacancy lines are shown.

notices.text: The rent roll is dated 01 October 2026, 51 days before the screen date. Ask for a current roll before relying on occupancy and expiries.
Tenants' security deposits of AED 204,500 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 28% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 37% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 35% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
Statement NOI moved -3.9% against the prior period (12 months to Sep 2025).

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Building condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age (MEP, lifts, facade, waterproofing).
Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences and VAT treatment of shop rents.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Pursue**: the building passes every mandate test, though the unlevered return clears its target by a thin margin.

Buy at AED 36.5m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], exit at 8.8% [[uw.exit_yield]]. Asking is AED 35.0m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], which is within our value. The assumption that most moves the walk-away price is the exit yield. A move of 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] either way shifts the price by AED 5.2m [[uw.walk_away_largest_swing_aed]]. The walk-away price and returns rest on the firm's house view (reference rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime), not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Lantana Court, International City (Phase 2, Warsan First), G+5, completed 2016 [[deal.completion_year]], 94 units [[om.unit_count]]. Freehold, single title.
- **Price:** AED 35.0m [[uw.price_aed]], which is AED 699 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA and AED 559 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]] on BUA.
- **Income:** in-place rent is AED 3.9m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] on direct leases, with no master tenant. Occupancy is 96% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] by units. The mix is 60 studios [[rr.studio.units]], 30 1BR [[rr.1br.units]] and 4 retail units [[rr.retail.units]]. Of the let units, 87 are occupied [[rr.status.occupied]], 2 are under renewal [[rr.status.under_renewal]] and 1 has had notice served [[rr.status.notice_served]].

## Returns
| Metric | Deal | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR, pre-tax | 7.9% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | at least 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] |
| Unlevered equity multiple, pre-tax | 1.39x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | at least 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 8.1% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | at least 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |

- Entry yield on price is 8.6% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]]. Exit yield is 8.8% [[uw.exit_yield]]. Year-1 NOI is AED 3.0m [[uw.noi_year1]].
- Levered, pre-tax (secondary): IRR 8.4% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]], multiple 1.44x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]]. Year-1 DSCR is 1.75x [[uw.dscr_year1]].
- The OM's headline yield is 8.3% [[om.yield_stated]], net on total cost. On the buyer's basis it is 8.1% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]], which is 0.3 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]] lower.

## What would make it fail
- **Rent:** with market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower at the base exit yield, unlevered IRR falls to 6.9% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], under the 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] target.
- **Exit yield:** at the base rent with the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, unlevered IRR is 6.9% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]]. With both shocks together it is 6.0% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]].
- **Expiry cluster:** 33% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of in-place rent, AED 1.3m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]], expires between 1 October 2026 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 31 December 2026 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. That is within the mandate limit but sits in a single quarter.
- **Income trend:** statement NOI fell 3.9% [[notice.statement_trend]] against the prior period. The screen's reference rent is above in-place rent, so over-renting is not the risk here.

## Discrepancies
The facts flag no document conflicts. The OM and the rent roll agree on units, rent, occupancy and price per sq ft. Two gaps matter:
- **OM yield:** the OM's 8.3% [[om.yield_stated]] reproduces on its own basis. The screen's Year-1 NOI is lower, so the buyer's yield on total cost is 8.1% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. It still passes the mandate.
- **NOI:** the statement shows NOI of AED 3.1m [[bridge.statement_noi_aed]] and the screen uses AED 3.0m [[bridge.screen_noi_year1_aed]]. The screen adds AED 80k [[bridge.step1]] of modelled lease income. It takes off AED 62k [[bridge.step2]] for vacancy and collection loss, AED 40k [[bridge.step3]] for the management fee, AED 23k [[bridge.step4]] for leasing fees and AED 9,968 [[bridge.step5]] for irrecoverable VAT.

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Checks before diligence
- Get a current rent roll. The one we have is 51 days [[notice.stale_rent_roll]] old. Confirm what happened to the leases in the three-month window with the most expiring rent.
- Reconcile the OM yield and the statement NOI to the screen's Year-1 NOI, and ask the seller to explain the NOI decline.
- Security deposits of AED 204,500 [[notice.security_deposits]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Cheque profile: 35% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is on the longest cheque schedules, which means more collection risk.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including buyer eligibility.
- Dubai Municipality completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
- Civil Defence certificates and ACP cladding compliance.
- Building condition survey and capex plan.
- Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences and VAT treatment.

## Assumptions
The exit yield is the higher of the area yield and the entry yield, plus 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion and an age premium, over a 5-year [[uw.hold_years]] hold. Market rent falls 1.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1, is flat in Year 2, then rises 2.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]], collection loss 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]] and renewal probability 70% [[assume.renewal_probability]]. The loan is 45% [[assume.max_ltv]] LTV, sized at 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] DSCR, at 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]] and amortising over 15 years [[assume.amortisation_years]]. No operating cost categories were filled from mandate defaults.
